title: How did you guys create assets with Claude?
author: MarcLabb
selftext:
Hey everyone! 

I have been working on a top down 2d souls like and i already have my base assets for the game but eould like more depth. I see in thread here that people have made crazy assets with claude, how did you manage? 

Just curious to see how everyone was working with Claude!

replies.author: MarcLabb
replies.body: Would be great! I just want to try something first, maybe in the future:)

comments.author: Blake9712
comments.body: I made an asset builder and I hand made most from there and then when u had enough assets created I asked Claude to make some in my asset builder and when it did it wrong I told it what was wrong until its Md was good enough. But essentially I spent like 3 months of usage credits making the asset builder

replies.author: MarcLabb
replies.body: Ok cool, so basically a lot of back and forth with claude until you get the desired asset, thanks !

replies.author: Blake9712
replies.body:
Yes. And then I can edit its asset in my asset editor. And it’s important Claude knows the design language in its MD. And it often bases assets on others. Also I can make my own assets. For mine I need so many assets that I had to make it easy but front loading that asset editor work was real hard. But these dk inspired assets were one shot and fine for my game. The retro no shading style I’m going for probably makes it easier since I’ve asked it not to overly detail anything   


https://preview.redd.it/qrfgf46luprh1.jpeg?width=1284&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=10562bf02b31313c2d7a54b3de5f85cb1e5fb172

comments.author: CraftyWitchInc
comments.body: MCPs often give it the tools they need. There's one for Aseprite and Blender. It also depends on how well in depth your prompt is and the tools the specific MCP provide. Helps if you have references readily available too. Just make sure to put emphasis on consistency.

replies.author: MarcLabb
replies.body: Will for sure look into that, thats really good. Thank you !

comments.author: zayelion
comments.body:
Only using Astra/Caude as the orchestrator.

I have specialized models for the asset creation process. I can do them by hand unless the idea is pretty simple and I need it to do the boileplating. I then go in and edit fields and regenerate the asset so it fits into the game properly instead of a rough form. Seperate specialized models do other generation and the frontier models just trigger them via API.

replies.author: tightsweatpants
replies.body: I mostly design them myself. I sometimes use Claude to scaffold an idea inside the pixel parameter I give it but it’s usually garbage but it gives me a boilerplate to edit instead of having to pixel from scratch.

comments.author: Outrageous-Issue9722
comments.body:
Opus 5.5 figured out that Blockbench has a debug port it can open and it made its own "mcp" to specifically work with my editor pipeline by making a blockbench plugin it can talk to/control the window.  It was pretty cool seeing it figure it out in real time.  It found it because I was having an issue with my IK doing a euler flip that I had it troubleshoot, and it was not observable through the logging it was doing.  Now it can make meshes, IK animations, etc in blockbench and export a screenshot strip showing specific key frames/camera orientations for the animations.  If you try the same thing, there is also a flag you can pass to disable background throttling, so it can do everything while it's minimized.

I explained it all like that because the screenshot strip would actually work very well for you to make 2d sprites/animations from 3d models.

comments.author: FazedEclipse2
comments.body:
Top down pixel art?

If so compile your design documents together and post into a claude chat. Opus high "make a video of this game in 2d pixel art style"

Then probe it, you built this entirely in code. Build a skill that helps an agent build like this in Godot. Install the skill. Ask the agent to design a plan to make your concept into a game in this coded pixel art style. Profit.

comments.author: RoutineOne2769
comments.body: From what I've seen work for 2D: generated sprite sheets drift between frames (outfit, proportions), so people either use a sprite tool through MCP (PixelLab gets mentioned a lot here) or build a simple 3D rig and render it to sprites, which keeps every frame consistent. Either way, get one character exactly right first and save that process as instructions, then reuse it.
